impact: Build the data foundations that help Netflix understand what hundreds of millions of devices can actually support — whether it's ads, live streaming, or a new UI — so product teams know exactly what they're rolling out to.

Analyze crash logs and startup performance across TVs, mobile, and Netflix Games to surface what's degrading the viewing experience — turning raw device telemetry into actionable improvements for users.
Map device capabilities like video resolution and audio support (4K, Dolby) so Netflix can tailor the streaming experience to what each device can actually deliver.
Work on cross-device ad experiences — like seamlessly stitching a TV session to a phone on the same profile — so ads transition smoothly without breaking the user's flow.
Surface education and upsell opportunities by identifying users whose devices support higher quality than their plan allows, or whose settings aren't taking full advantage of what they're paying for.
Help distinguish personal devices from shared ones like hotel or Airbnb TVs — because a hotel lobby TV and your living room TV shouldn't have the same login experience or feature rollout.
Mapped out Twilio's entire growth funnel — from first website visit to signup to activation — so the growth team could see exactly where users dropped off and what drove conversions.
Built the data behind Monthly Active Developer Accounts and uncovered how developers actually used Twilio — as a direct tool vs. an embedded API — helping shape who Twilio was building for.
Enabled marketing to measure real campaign performance against signups, not just impressions — connecting spend to actual user growth.
Partnered with finance to build revenue pipelines for monthly, quarterly, and yearly reporting — where accuracy wasn't optional.

Partnered with customer service and operations teams to build data pipelines that surfaced key metrics — case resolution times, ticket trends, and escalation patterns — helping the team respond faster to healthcare providers.

Built pipelines to track operational throughput — analysis turnaround times, case volumes, and provider adoption — giving the ops team visibility into how efficiently cardiovascular analyses were being delivered to cardiologists.

Helped enterprise customers design and implement end-to-end data systems with HP Vertica at the core — not just setting up a database, but architecting the full data warehouse solution around their needs.
Built streaming data pipelines using Kafka and Spark to get real-time data flowing into Vertica for analytics — giving customers a modern data infrastructure they could grow with.

Built a data quality framework for financial investment data — an end-to-end application that scored data assets against prioritized rules, so investment bankers could trust the data driving their decisions.
Designed custom rule-based exception handling that flagged bad data automatically, turning a manual review process into something repeatable and reliable for enterprise-scale financial workflows.
